service.description: The route groups a device may be registered for (moqui.security.DeviceRouteGroup, each owner's seed data): its description and owner, the parameter a registration fixes (a wall display's playlist) and its default idle timeout and lifetime. A row naming a missing artifact group is logged by name and left out. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

The registered devices, newest first: name, route group and its fixed parameter, display account, site, who registered it and when, when and from which address it was last seen (a client summary, never the user agent), and its state (pending, codeExpired, active, stopped, revoked) with the reason; never a code, a secret or a hash. Ended ones (revoked, stopped, a code not entered in time) only with includeEnded or a state. With displayUserIdList (the accounts in a caller's identity scope) only those accounts' devices are listed and the others counted (otherCount), never named. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

Registers one device for a registered route group, to run as a display account: the registration code is returned once (registrationCode, about 99 bits, good once within codeMinutes: 15 by default, 5 to 60) and kept only as its hash; it is entered on the device, whose browser then holds the credential. Refused, as a reason, for an unregistered route group, a missing required parameter, an account that is not a display account fit for a device (displayAccount Y, no password or external identity, not disabled, in no privileged group, holding no sealed permission) or one in a group the registrar could not assign (AccessServices' delegation rules). The device stops when not seen for idleTimeoutMinutes (the route group's default, a week; 5 to 43200) or after lifetimeDays (365; at most 730), and may be held to ipAllowed. A retry with the same operationKey answers the first registration without a code. The registration is evidence in the audit log. The framework knows no organization: the caller scopes the display account. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

parameter.description: False for a screen: the registration is made without a code, and issue#DeviceCode makes it at the render that shows it, so no request, session or message carries it from the write to the page

parameter.name: registrationCode
parameter.description: Shown once; never stored, logged or listed

service.description: The registration code of a device registered without one (register#Device with issueCode false), made as it is shown: once, to the administrator who registered the device, within fifteen minutes of the registration, and kept only as its hash. Refused, as a reason, for another administrator's registration, a device already in use or ended, a code already shown, or a registration left too long. Showing it is evidence in the audit log. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

parameter.name: registrationCode
parameter.description: Shown once; never stored, logged or listed

service.description: Revokes a device at once, on every server: every request of a device reads its registration, so its next one is refused and its cookie removed, and no web session holds its identity to end beside it. A revoked device stays revoked (it is registered again for a new code); revoking it again answers the first revocation, so no revision is asked for. Evidence in the audit log with the reason. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

Makes the browser of the request under way the device of a registration code: once, before the code expires. The device's cookie goes on the response (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure on https) and is given to no script; any user signed in on the browser's session is signed out. A code that is unknown, used, expired or revoked gets one answer, is counted by the web protection (which slows and blocks an address that guesses) and, when it was a registration's, leaves evidence in the audit log. homePath is the route group's own.
What the browser of the request under way is registered as, for the device page: its name and the path its route group opens at; nothing else of the registration.
